deep.reconstruction:
Heading: 'Litt: Z. Zu der Berechnung der Secularstörungen gehörig' (belonging to the computation of the secular perturbations). This is the problem behind Gauss's ring method (Determinatio attractionis, 1818). The disturbing planet's mass is smeared over its orbit in proportion to time, i.e. to mean anomaly. One then needs integrals over the eccentric anomaly E of powers of the distance from a fixed point to the moving point of the ellipse.

(1) Setup. The squared distance from a fixed point to the ellipse point (a cos E - ae, b sin E, 0) is a trigonometric polynomial of degree 2 in E. Gauss writes the distance as
 r = M sqrt{(1 - α cos(E+A))(1 - b cos(E+B))}.
The normalisation A + B = 0 is achieved by shifting the origin of E. The constants may in general be complex; the page does not discuss this.

(2) Goal. Put u = E + B and Δ = A - B, so that E + A = u + Δ. Also put R = α² + b² - 2αb cosΔ. Gauss wants to write
 (1 - α cos(u+Δ)) / (1 - b cos u) = [1 - αb cosΔ + sqrt(R - α²b² sin²Δ) cos θ] / (1 - b²).
He states the resulting closed forms:
• cos θ = [b(α cosΔ - b) - (α cosΔ - b) cos u + α(1-b²) sinΔ sin u] / [(1 - b cos u) sqrt(R - α²b² sin²Δ)].
• sin θ = sqrt(1-b²) [αb sinΔ - α sinΔ cos u - (α cosΔ - b) sin u] / [(1 - b cos u) sqrt(R - α²b² sin²Δ)].
• The linear combination (α cosΔ - b) cos θ + α sqrt(1-b²) sinΔ sin θ = sqrt(R - α²b² sin²Δ) (b - cos u)/(1 - b cos u).

(3) A cheaper route. Gauss remarks: 'Man hätte die Verwandlung wohlfeilern Kaufs gehabt, wenn man sofort gesetzt hätte' (one would have got the transformation more cheaply by setting at once)
 tan(V/2) = sqrt((1+b)/(1-b)) tan(u/2) = T.
This is the eccentric-to-true-anomaly relation for an 'eccentricity' b.
• With t = tan(u/2), cos u = (1-t²)/(1+t²) and sin u = 2t/(1+t²), the ratio becomes [1 + t² - α cosΔ (1-t²) + 2α sinΔ t] / [1 + t² - b + b t²].
• Substituting t² = (1-b)/(1+b) T² gives the next expression on the page.
• Mine: the denominator equals (1-b)(1+T²). Dividing by it gives
 ratio = [(1+b)(1-α cosΔ) cos²(V/2) + (1-b)(1+α cosΔ) sin²(V/2) + α sinΔ sqrt(1-b²) sin V] / (1-b²).
• Halving the angles gives
 ratio = [1 - αb cosΔ + (b - α cosΔ) cos V + α sinΔ sqrt(1-b²) sin V] / (1-b²).
• Mine: the amplitude of the last two terms is (b - α cosΔ)² + α² sin²Δ (1-b²) = R - α²b² sin²Δ. Hence θ = V - φ with cos φ = (b - α cosΔ)/sqrt(...) and sin φ = α sinΔ sqrt(1-b²)/sqrt(...). This reproduces the cos θ and sin θ formulas of (2), using cos V = (cos u - b)/(1 - b cos u) and sin V = sqrt(1-b²) sin u/(1 - b cos u).

(4) Differentials. Gauss notes dV/sin V = dE/sin(E+B); the page writes sin E loosely for sin u. He also gives dE/dV = sin(E+B)/sin V = (1 - b cos(E+B))/sqrt(1-b²).

(5) Purpose (mine, implicit). Write P = 1 - αb cosΔ and Q = sqrt(R - α²b² sin²Δ). Then dE/r = dV/[M sqrt(1-b²) sqrt(ratio)] = dθ/[M sqrt(P + Q cos θ)]. So integrals over the orbit of r^(-1), r^(-3), etc. reduce to complete elliptic integrals of the form ∫ dθ (P + Q cos θ)^(-n/2). Gauss evaluated such integrals by the arithmetic-geometric mean.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Every displayed identity checks out under the sign convention θ = V - φ.
Notational slip: dV/sin V = ∂E/sin E should read dE/sin(E+B), i.e. du/sin u with u = E+B. The next line uses sin(E+B) correctly.
Grouping: in the sin θ formula the denominator is written 1 - b cos(E+B)·sqrt(...) without brackets. The intended denominator is (1 - b cos(E+B))·sqrt(...).
Unaddressed point: the factorisation of the quadratic trigonometric polynomial into two real linear factors with A+B=0 can require complex α, b, A. The page passes over this silently.

results.what: Representation of the point-to-ellipse distance as M·sqrt((1-α cos(E+A))(1-b cos(E+B))) and transformation of the ratio of the two factors into (P + Q cos θ)/(1-b²), with explicit cos θ and sin θ.
results.modern_name: Reduction of the Gaussian ring (secular perturbation) integral to a complete elliptic integral
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Determinatio attractionis (1818); later reworked by Hill (1882), Halphen and Goriachev

results.what: Substitution tan(V/2) = sqrt((1+b)/(1-b)) tan(u/2), which linearises 1/(1-b cos u) and gives dE/(1-b cos u) = dV/sqrt(1-b²).
results.modern_name: Eccentric-to-true anomaly (Kepler) substitution; Weierstrass/tangent half-angle substitution

results.what: Amplitude identity (b - α cosΔ)² + α² sin²Δ (1-b²) = α² + b² - 2αb cosΔ - α²b² sin²Δ.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the reduction used in Gauss's own ring method for secular perturbations, which is well known to be his. The particular route via the true-anomaly substitution of the second factor is a variant of his 1818 published derivation and a nice Nachlass detail. It is not a new result.

checkable.asserts: Numerator in the half-angle variable t.
Denominator in the half-angle variable t.
The ratio in T equals [1 - αb cosΔ + (b - α cosΔ) cos V + α sinΔ sqrt(1-b²) sin V]/(1-b²). Take 0<b<1.
The squared amplitude equals R - α²b² sin²Δ.
Gauss's cos θ formula: sqrt(...)·cos θ in terms of u = E+B.
Gauss's sin θ formula, with θ = V - φ.
dV/du = sqrt(1-b²)/(1-b cos u), equivalently dE/dV = (1 - b cos(E+B))/sqrt(1-b²) and dV/sin V = du/sin u.
